requiredFindings.title: Mark the unwind kill before attempting the reap so its confirmation is retained
requiredFindings.detail: The loop path fixes round-1 RF-9, but unwind still sends SIGKILL and calls try_reap before setting ladder.kill_at (1839-1855). try_reap captures tree_confirmed only when kill_at is already present (1710-1712). Therefore Drop from Handshaking or Running can successfully reap a root-only child with no saved confirmation. unwind then sets kill_at and settle falls back to confirm_tree after reap (1742-1744), when the root-only group is empty. This reports Incomplete for a successfully killed root-only group and performs the by-pid confirmation after losing the zombie-root hold. The new tree-report test covers the normal fault loop, while the Drop tests check group/scratch cleanup but not this report.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Record the unwind kill state before the first reap attempt, or explicitly capture the same pre-reap confirmation on every unwind reap path. Reuse that observation in settlement; never fall back to a by-pid confirmation after a successful reap. Add Drop/unwind controls from Handshaking and Running that inspect the resulting tree report (or a test seam capturing the settlement), including root-only and missed-member cases.

requiredFindings.title: Close handle admission atomically with the final settlement drain
requiredFindings.detail: The settled flag check and try_send are separate operations. A sender can observe false at :488, pause, let settle set the flag and drain the channel at :1797-1802, then resume and enqueue successfully at :492. Public run has already stopped servicing the receiver, so this trigger is neither merged nor counted as late; host_fault returns true and late_events remains unchanged. Acquire/Release ordering does not make the check/send pair atomic. The new public test sends only after run has returned and therefore misses this interleaving. The sequential late-send case is fixed, but the cross-thread lifecycle guarantee remains incomplete.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Give handle admission and settlement closing/draining one synchronization or linearization protocol, so every accepted pre-close trigger is accounted for and every post-close request is rejected/counts exactly once without a consumer turn. Preserve bounded nonblocking trigger handling. Add a deterministic concurrent control using barriers around the pre-send check and settlement close, and assert the return value, final count and absence of an unaccounted queued trigger.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Carry the health-refusal provenance into the deferred record owner
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The supervisor now classifies the health nonce mismatch correctly, but its comment says the RF7 refusal is kept as evidence. receive_control consumes that RefusedFrame and emits only LivenessMissed plus the Liveness trigger; ControlSession retains state/sequence/stopping information, not that refusal detail. The observer API has no explicit refused-frame event. This is distinct from the expiry path, but the typed family/detail itself is not handed onward.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestedChange: When D3a-3 adds the record projection, preserve an explicit reduced host-held discriminator for nonce mismatch versus window expiry and the control-owner refusal family, without retaining nonce/frame/detail text. Clarify the current comment so it does not claim a retained evidence object that the API drops.
